_doc: FACT-HARVEST constructions (graph data — the agent's construction grammar). These extend the harvesting machinery to capture the OBJECT-LEVEL facts HLE needs from arXiv frontier prose — the detail nLab LACKED (147 computed-invariant pages of 19,097). Two families, each a list of slot PATTERNS (NOT hand-coded per-fact, NOT an LLM): a pattern is regex-anchored markers around object/value slots; the harvester (construction_grammar.harvest_facts) applies whichever patterns are seeded and emits {object, invariant_kind, value} / {object, relation, target} fact rows. Teaching a new fact shape = adding a pattern here (graph data), not writing code. The patterns read the LaTeX-PRESERVED rendered prose (stacks/nlab-style render: '\cong' -> 'isomorphic to', '\mathbb{Z}' -> 'Z', 'H_n(X)' / 'H^k(X)' / 'pi_n(X)' survive). HONEST: the precision is the residual variable — author prose is noisy (hypotheses, 'if ... then', variable invariants); the patterns are deliberately ANCHORED (a named homology/cohomology/homotopy operator on the object side, a copula/iso marker, a concrete group/value on the value side) to favour precision over recall; report the measured precision.
_doc_invariants: COMPUTED INVARIANTS: an object's homology/cohomology/homotopy/bordism/K-group/Euler-characteristic/rank/dimension COMPUTED to a concrete value. The invariant-kind operator (H_n / H^k / pi_n / chi / rank) is the ANCHOR on the object side; an iso/equality marker ('isomorphic to' [from \cong], 'is', '=', 'equals') joins it to a concrete VALUE (a group Z / Z/k / Q / a number / a named group). The `object` is the invariant applied to a space; the `value` is the computed answer. These are the rows nLab almost entirely lacked.

invariants.name: homology_iso
invariants._doc: 'H_n(X) isomorphic to Z' / 'H^2(X) = Z/2' -> object=H_n(X), kind=homology, value=Z. The object_re captures a homology/cohomology operator H_<dim>(<space>); the value is the concrete group/number up to a clause boundary.

invariants.name: homotopy_iso
invariants._doc: 'pi_1(X) isomorphic to Z' -> object=pi_1(X), kind=homotopy, value=Z. The homotopy-group computation.

invariants.name: named_group_of_is
invariants._doc: PROSE form 'the [homology/cohomology/...] group of X is G' -> object='[kind] group of X', kind=<group_kind>, value=G. group 1 is the invariant-kind word, group 2 the object, then the value. The form the prompt names explicitly.

invariants.name: rank_is
invariants._doc: 'the rank of H_2(X) is 3' -> object='rank of H_2(X)', kind=rank, value=3. A computed numeric rank.

invariants.name: euler_char_is
invariants._doc: 'the Euler characteristic of X is -2' -> object='euler characteristic of X', kind=euler_characteristic, value=-2.

_doc_identifications: IDENTIFICATIONS: an object IDENTIFIED with another object — homeomorphic / diffeomorphic / isomorphic / equivalent / 'can be identified with' / 'is the classifying space of'. The relation marker is the ANCHOR; the two slots are the two objects. These are the rows nLab DOES have (1,623) — here they flow from arXiv too, joining the description->object grounding (an identification lets the analysis-by-synthesis loop reach an object it lacked).

identifications.name: homeomorphic_to
identifications._doc: 'X is homeomorphic to Y' -> X --homeomorphic--> Y.

identifications.name: diffeomorphic_to
identifications._doc: 'X is diffeomorphic to Y' -> X --diffeomorphic--> Y.

identifications.name: isomorphic_to_object
identifications._doc: 'G is isomorphic to H' -> G --isomorphic--> H. (NB: the homology/homotopy iso forms above are mined as invariants; this catches OBJECT-to-OBJECT isomorphism — e.g. group identifications.)

identifications.name: identified_with
identifications._doc: 'X can be identified with Y' -> X --identified_with--> Y.

identifications.name: equivalent_to
identifications._doc: 'X is (homotopy) equivalent to Y' -> X --equivalent--> Y.

identifications.name: classifying_space_of
identifications._doc: 'X is the classifying space of G' -> X --classifying_space_of--> G (the BG identification).
